overview.overview:
Nebraska's 1st Congressional District, which awards one electoral vote, is forecast to lean Republican. Republican candidates carried it by 14.92 points in 2020 and by 12.97 points in 2024, and it runs well to the right of the national average. The forecast projects a high single-digit Republican margin, with a range that includes a narrow Democratic result at the far edge.

The district is unlikely to decide the national outcome. Its single electoral vote would not affect the result in any realistic scenario. Don Bacon, a Republican, is listed among the home-state candidates. No district-level polling is currently available.
overview.watch: A sustained move toward Democrats in Nebraska's suburban and Omaha-area precincts, or a strong local candidate or poll showing a close race, would be the clearest signal that the outlook could change.
key_factors: Republican candidates won the district by roughly 13 to 15 points in both 2020 and 2024.
The district leans well to the right of the nation, which keeps the projected margin Republican.
The national environment adjustment is modest and does not shift the district's partisan lean enough to change its expected result.
No district polls or recent headlines are available to suggest a shift.
